tools.name: create_inbox
tools.description: Get a public URL that records every HTTP request sent to it, plus the inbox_key that all other tools need. Use it as a webhook endpoint, OAuth redirect URI, job callback URL, or with create_approval_link. The key is shown only once: keep it.

tools.name: get_inbox
tools.description: Show an inbox: its URL, expiry, request count, latest request id, configured responses and approval links.

tools.name: list_requests
tools.description: List captured requests as summaries, oldest first. Without "after" you get the most recent ones; with "after" you page forward from that request id. Use get_request for headers and body. Does not move wait_for_request's position.

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: Full details of one captured request: method, path, parsed query, headers, body (UTF-8 text or base64), plus "json" or "form" when the body parses. tools.name: wait_for_request
tools.description: Block until a request arrives, then return it in full (same shape as get_request). By default it returns the next request not yet returned by wait_for_request for this inbox and these filters, so nothing that arrives between calls is missed, including requests that came in before the first call. tools.name: set_response
tools.description: Choose what Porch sends back to callers, for the whole inbox or a sub-path: status, headers and body. tools.name: create_approval_link
tools.description: Make a link to send a person when you need their decision ("Deploy to production?"). It opens a page with your title, message and one button per choice. Only a button press counts, so link previews and email scanners cannot answer by accident, only the first answer is accepted, and opening the page

tools.name: wait_for_approval
tools.description: Block until the person answers an approval link, then return their choice. Returns at once if it was already answered. On timeout, call it again.

tools.name: clear_requests
tools.description: Delete all captured requests from the inbox. The URL, key and response settings stay the same.

tools.name: delete_inbox
tools.description: Delete the inbox and everything it captured. Its URL starts returning 404 and the key stops working.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_inbox, get_inbox · Private data: create_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, list_requests, set_response, create_approval_link · Destructive: set_response, clear_requests, delete_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_inbox, get_inbox · Private data: create_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, list_requests, set_response, create_approval_link · Destructive: set_response, clear_requests, delete_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
